get_employee.description: Read one employee's details by their HiBob employee ID or email address: name, email, job title, department, site, start date, and their manager's name and email. HiBob has no standard probation field: if your company added one, name it in Fields, or use "List employees with a date in a period".

parameters.description: The HiBob fields to return, by field ID, such as root.email or work.department (List employee fields shows every ID). Leave blank for HiBob's standard set: the employee's name and email and the About, Employment and Work sections. A field your company added, such as a probation end date, only comes back when it is named here. HiBob leaves out, without an error, any field the connected service user may not view.

schema.description: The HiBob fields to return, by field ID, such as root.email or work.department (List employee fields shows every ID). Leave blank for HiBob's standard set: the employee's name and email and the About, Employment and Work sections. activity.description: Defines whether an employee that requests time off would have the leave defined as: paidTimeoff (Not working, paid): typically for paid vacation, paid sick, and parental leave. unpaidTimeoff (Not working, unpaid): typically for when an employees has used all of their paid time off balance, but still needs to take time off. workTime (Working): typically for working from home (WFH) or business travel.

currentAssignment.description: This field indicates whether the employee is actively assigned to the policy type on the date the balance is requested. Unassigned means the employee is not actively assigned to the policy type on the requested date. Balance values may still reflect amounts accrued while the employee was previously assigned.

startingBalance.description: The balance as of the cycle start date.

totalAdminAdjustments.description: Total number of days/hours manually adjusted.

totalBalanceAsOfDate.description: The retrieved balance as of this date.

totalRoundedBalanceAsOfDate.description: The retrieved rounded balance as of this date.

Change in behavior starting November 20, 2024: From this date, the bookingWorkDaysOnly setting has moved from the Policy Type to the Policy details. Policies that were created before this date will return the original value from the policy type.

maxBalance.description: Maximum balance at the end of the cycle.

minTimeOffRequestDuration.description: The shortest amount of time employees can request.

yearsOfService.description: Start after this number of years.

get_time_off_request.description: Get the details of one time off request: its dates, length, status and who approved it.
get_time_off_request.name: get_time_off_request

parameters.description: The employee who asked for the time off: pick one, or give their HiBob employee ID.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: The time off request's number, which List whos out returns as requestId.
parameters.name: request_id

parameters.description: Include a day-by-day breakdown of the request. On by default.
parameters.name: include_daily_durations

approved.description: Whether the request is approved (and hence publicly visible).

createdOn.description: The date and time the time off request was created.

durationUnit.description: The unit used for the totalDuration and totalCost - either 'days' or 'hours'

durations.description: Daily durations of the time off request with cost per day.

items.description: Daily durations entry with date and cost.

cost.description: The cost deducted from balance for this day.

date.description: The date in the time off request range.

endDate.description: Date of the last day of the time off.

endPortion.description: What portion of the last day is included - all_day, morning or afternoon (relevant for requests using the days type).

originalRequestId.description: The ID of the very first time-off request. It remains unchanged regardless of updates that create new time off request records. It serves as the anchor for tracing the request's entire history back to its initial submission.

policyTypeCustomName.description: The custom public-facing label when the policy's visibility is Custom name; null for Public and Private policies. Never contains sensitive information. Always returned regardless of caller permissions.

policyTypeDisplayName.description: The policy type name returned for this request. May contain sensitive information, such as the original policy type name for Private policies or when the caller has permission on Custom name policies. When policyTypeCustomName is not null and differs from this value, this field contains the original policy type name, meaning the caller has permission to see it.

previousRequestId.description: The ID of the previous request that was replaced when this new request was created. This occurs when the request's date or time is updated, resulting in a new time off request record.

reasonCode.description: The reason given for the request, from the policy type's list of reason codes.

startDate.description: Date of the first day of the time off.

startPortion.description: What portion of the first day is included - all_day, morning or afternoon (relevant for requests using the days type).

status.description: Request status. This can be approved, pending, canceled, etc.

timeZoneOffset.description: Calculated time zone offset from GMT in ±HH:MM format (e.g., "GMT -5:00"). This field is relevant only for time-off requests which allow specifying exact start and end times (e.g., 09:00–18:00). The value is automatically calculated based on the employee's assigned site time zone.

totalCost.description: The amount that will be deducted from the balance

totalDuration.description: The total amount of time the request covers, including regular days off such as weekends

type.description: The type of request - days is when the request is for X days.

visibility.description: The request visibility either 'Public', 'Private' or 'Custom name'

list_employees_by_date.description: Find the employees whose probation ends, who start work, or who have a work anniversary this month, next month or between two dates. Each comes back as one ready-to-read record with their name, email, job title, department, start date, probation end date, and their manager's name and email, so reminding each manager needs no further lookups. HiBob has no standard probation field: the probation end date is read from the date field your company added for it, found by the word "probation" in its name.
list_employees_by_date.display_name: List employees with a date in a period
list_employees_by_date.display_str_template: List employees with a date in a period.
list_employees_by_date.name: list_employees_by_date

parameters.description: Which date to look for. Probation ends: the employee's probation end date falls in the period. Start date: the employee starts work in the period. Work anniversary: the day and month the employee started falls in the period, in a later year.
parameters.name: date_type

parameters.description: When the date must fall. Leave blank for this month, or for the dates in From and To when those are filled in. Months are calendar months in the workflow owner's time zone, so a run at 9:00 on the 1st gets the month that has just begun.
parameters.name: period

parameters.description: The first day of the period, for Between two dates.
parameters.name: from_date

parameters.description: The last day of the period, for Between two dates. At most a year after From.
parameters.name: to_date

parameters.description: Usually left blank: this month and next month are counted in the workflow owner's time zone. Give a time zone by name, such as Australia/Sydney or America/New_York, to count them somewhere else. UTC is used only when this is blank and the owner has no time zone saved.
parameters.name: timezone

parameters.description: Usually left blank: the probation end date is read from the one date field in your HiBob account with "probation" in its name. Pick the field here when your company calls it something else, or has more than one.
parameters.name: probation_field

hibob_employee_leaving_trigger.description: Beta. Runs once for an employee when a termination (their last day) is logged for them in HiBob, however far ahead it is dated, and again only if that date changes. Each run has who is leaving, their last day, the reason, and their manager's name and work email, so a workflow can ask the manager to confirm without looking anyone up. Terminations already logged when the workflow is turned on don't start it (held for the last day, only those whose last day has already gone by don't), and neither does one dated more than 30 days in the past. The HiBob service user needs View and View history on the Lifecycle table, and access to people who have left. To act on the last day itself (close an account, collect a laptop), set 'When to run' rather than adding a wait step: a wait can't be longer than 30 days, and a last day is often logged further ahead. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.department: The employee's department, such as Finance. Blank when they have none.
output.employee_email: The employee's work email address, such as ada@example.com, which is also how other apps usually know them. Blank when HiBob has none.
output.employee_id: The employee's HiBob ID, such as 3332883884017713938, for a HiBob step's Employee field.
output.employee_name: The employee's full name, such as Ada Lovelace.
output.employee_url: A link that opens the employee in HiBob. Blank for a connection to a HiBob sandbox.
output.first_name: The employee's first name, such as Ada.
output.job_title: The employee's job title, such as Accountant. Blank when they have none.
output.last_day: The termination date logged in HiBob, as a date such as 2026-12-22: the employee's last day of employment. To act on this day itself, set the trigger's 'When to run' to on_last_day or after_last_day rather than waiting until this date: a wait step can't be longer than 30 days.
output.last_day_display: The last day written for a message, such as Dec 22, 2026, so no step has to format it.
output.last_name: The employee's surname, such as Lovelace.
output.manager_email: Their manager's work email address, such as grace@example.com, ready to use as the approver of a 'Request approval' step. Blank when they have no manager.
output.manager_id: Their manager's HiBob ID, for a HiBob step's Employee field. Blank when they have no manager.
output.manager_name: The name of the employee's manager (who they report to in HiBob), such as Grace Hopper. Blank when they have no manager.
output.reason: The kind of reason logged with the termination, such as Resignation, as HiBob names it. Blank when none was chosen.
output.reason_note: The note typed with the termination, if any. Blank when there is none.
output.site: The site (office) the employee belongs to, such as London. Blank when they have none.

parameters.description: Beta. When the run starts. Leave empty (or enter when_logged) to start as soon as the last day is logged in HiBob, which can be weeks before it: right for asking a manager to confirm or planning a handover. Enter on_last_day to start as the last day begins (just after midnight), for a goodbye message or collecting a laptop. Enter after_last_day to start once the last day is over (just after the next midnight), for closing accounts without cutting off someone's final day. The last two use the termination as it stands that day, so a date that was moved or a termination that was cancelled never runs on the old date, and they read the date in the time zone of whoever turned the workflow on (UTC if they have none saved). Choose one of them instead of adding a wait step: a wait can't be longer than 30 days, and a last day is often logged further ahead.
parameters.name: run_when
